2. Detect cycles (A→B→C→A) and peel chains (descending amounts hop-by-hop) in the counterparty graph.
3. Compute total volume into/out of cycle members; compare to declared volume.

statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) requires financial institutions to report suspicious activity that may involve money laundering or other criminal activity. The fact pattern describes a business with a high declared monthly volume ($5,550,519) and a series of 21 transactions, many of which are large wire transfers to various LLCs (e.g., $1,580,009.82 to RC Associates LLC, $1,465,555.91 to PXJ Imports LLC). The high frequency and volume of these transfers to multiple entities are indicative of suspicious activity that should be reported under 5318(g).
